title: Rust: Channels and Message Passing
description: Use std::sync::mpsc channels for message passing between threads.

steps.title: Send and Receive
steps.description: Create a channel with `mpsc::channel()`. Spawn a thread that sends a message. Receive it in main and print.
hints: Spawn thread, move `tx` in, send a string.

verification.failureMessage: Send a message through the channel and print it.

steps.title: Multiple Messages
steps.description: Create a channel. Spawn a thread that sends 5 messages (1 through 5). In main, receive all 5 and print each one.
hints: Send in a loop: `for i in 1..=5 { tx.send(i).unwrap(); }`
Receive in a loop: `for received in rx { println!("{}", received); }`
The receiver iterator ends when the sender is dropped.

steps.title: Multiple Senders
steps.description: Create multiple sender threads sharing the same receiver. Use `mpsc::Sender` clones. Spawn 3 threads, each sending 3 messages. Receive and print all 9.
hints: Clone the sender for each thread: `let tx2 = tx.clone();`.
Drop the original sender in main so the receiver knows when to stop.
Receive in a loop: `for msg in rx { println!("{}", msg); }`

steps.title: Worker Pool Pattern
steps.description: Implement a worker pool: create a channel of jobs (integers). Spawn 3 worker threads that receive jobs and print `"Worker N processed job M"`. Send 10 jobs.
hints: Send job numbers through the channel.
Each worker loops, receives, and processes.
Use `Arc<...>` if sharing state, or clone the receiver.

verification.failureMessage: Print each worker processing a job.

steps.title: Bounded Channel (SyncChannel)
steps.description: Create a bounded channel with `mpsc::sync_channel(3)` (capacity 3). Spawn a producer that sends 10 items and a consumer that receives them. Demonstrate backpressure by printing when send blocks.
hints: `sync_channel(3)` creates a channel with buffer size 3.
When the buffer is full, `send()` blocks until the consumer receives.
Print timing messages to show backpressure.

verification.failureMessage: Send 10 items through a bounded channel of capacity 3.
